## 1. Executive Summary

This document governs the structural and tax-planning decisions for the transaction. It records the selected deal form, tax elections, rollover and earnout mechanics, and the sequenced step-plan required to close. All open items are tracked with owners and ETAs; risk ratings follow the RED / AMBER / GREEN (RAG) convention.

---

## 2. Structure Selection Matrix

### 2.1 Options Analysed

| Criterion | Asset Purchase | Stock Purchase | Forward Merger | Reverse Merger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Tax basis step-up (Buyer)** | ✅ Full step-up | ❌ Carryover basis | ✅ (if §338 elected) | ✅ (if §338(h)(10) elected) |
| **Seller tax cost** | ❌ Higher (ordinary income on recapture) | ✅ Capital gains rate | ✅ Capital gains rate | ✅ Capital gains rate |
| **Liability assumption** | ✅ Selective | ❌ All liabilities transfer | ❌ All liabilities transfer | ❌ All liabilities transfer |
| **Contract / consent complexity** | ❌ High (novation required) | ✅ Low | ✅ Low | ✅ Low |
| **State transfer taxes** | ❌ May apply per asset | ✅ Generally exempt | ✅ Generally exempt | ✅ Generally exempt |
| **IP / license transfer risk** | ❌ Change-of-control in each agreement | ✅ Survives in entity | ✅ Survives in entity | ✅ Survives in entity |
| **Complexity / timeline** | Medium | Low | Medium | Medium |

### 2.2 Recommended Structure

**→ Stock Purchase with §338(h)(10) Election (if Target is an S-Corp or subsidiary) OR Reverse Triangular Merger (if Target is a C-Corp with significant third-party contracts)**

**Rationale:**
- Buyer achieves economic equivalent of an asset step-up while preserving Target's legal entity, minimising contract novation risk.
- Seller stockholders receive capital-gains treatment on the entire purchase price, reducing blended tax cost vs. a straight asset deal.
- A Reverse Triangular Merger (RTM) uses a newly formed Merger Sub; Target survives as a wholly owned subsidiary, keeping all permits, licences, and customer contracts intact by operation of law.
- If Target is an S-Corp or QSub, a §338(h)(10) election achieves a deemed asset purchase for tax while maintaining the stock-deal legal form.

**Decision owner:** CFO + Tax Counsel
**Decision deadline:** 2026-10-17
**Status:** 🟡 AMBER — pending final tax-basis analysis and seller consent

## 3. Tax Elections

### 3.1 §338(h)(10) Election (S-Corp / Subsidiary Targets)

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Eligibility** | Target must be an S-Corp or 80%-owned subsidiary of a consolidated group |
| **Filing deadline** | IRS Form 8023 — due by the 15th day of the 9th month after the acquisition month (or by the due date of the return for the acquisition year, if earlier) |
| **Joint filing requirement** | Both Buyer and Seller must sign Form 8023 |
| **Effect** | Target is treated as having sold all assets in a taxable transaction, then liquidated; Buyer receives stepped-up basis |
| **Seller impact** | Single level of tax (no double tax for S-Corp); gain recognised at shareholder level |
| **Buyer impact** | Full fair-market-value basis in all Target assets, including goodwill and intangibles |
| **Owner** | Tax Counsel (Lead) + CFO |
| **ETA** | Election form prepared: 2026-11-07; executed at Closing |
| **RAG** | 🟢 GREEN |

### 3.2 §754 / §743(b) Step-Up Election (if Target is a Partnership or LLC Taxed as Partnership)

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Applicable if any portion of consideration is allocated to partnership interests |
| **Effect** | Adjusts inside basis of partnership assets to reflect Buyer's outside basis |
| **Filing** | Statement attached to partnership return for year of transfer |

## 4. Rollover Equity Mechanics

### 4.1 Structure Overview

Seller management and key stockholders will roll a portion of their equity proceeds into NewCo (or Buyer HoldCo) to align incentives post-close and achieve tax deferral.

```
Pre-Close                        Post-Close
─────────                        ──────────
Seller Stockholders              Buyer HoldCo
     │                           ├── Buyer Equity (80%)
     └─ 100% Target Equity       └── Rollover Equity (20%) ← former Sellers
                                          │
                                      Target (wholly owned sub)
```

### 4.2 Rollover Percentage & Sizing

| Parameter | Proposed |
|---|---|
| Rollover % of total equity value | 15–25% (to be negotiated) |
| Form | Preferred or common units / shares in Buyer HoldCo |
| Valuation basis | Same per-share/unit price as cash consideration |
| Minimum rollover threshold | Per Buyer: ensures key management retention |
| Maximum rollover threshold | Per Seller: ensures sufficient cash liquidity |

### 4.3 Tax Treatment of Rollover

- **Non-recognition:** Rollover investors do not recognise gain at Closing on exchanged shares, provided the transaction qualifies under IRC §368 (reorganisation) or §721 (partnership contribution). IRC §351 applies if structured as a C-Corp contribution.
- **Basis carryover:** Rollover investors carry their historic tax basis into the new equity; gain deferred until ultimate disposition.
- **Boot:** Any cash received alongside rolled equity is taxable as boot (§356); structure must minimise inadvertent boot.
- **Holding period:** Tacks for capital-gains purposes if qualifying exchange.
- **Condition:** Tax counsel must confirm that rollover does not cause "significant holder" issues under §368(a)(1)(B) continuity-of-interest rules.

### 4.4 Rollover Agreement Key Terms

| Term | Position |
|---|---|
| Lock-up period | 18–36 months post-Closing |
| Tag-along rights | Pro-rata on any Buyer exit |
| Drag-along obligations | Required to sell on exit at same terms |
| Put/call option | Buyer call at Year 3 at predetermined formula; Seller put on breach of fundamental reps |
| Anti-dilution | Broad-based weighted average |
| Information rights | Quarterly financials; annual audit |
| Board representation | 1 observer seat if rollover ≥ 20% |

- **Owner:** M&A Counsel (lead) + Tax Counsel
- **ETA:** Term sheet to Seller: 2026-10-17; Rollover Agreement execution: at Closing
- **RAG:** 🟡 AMBER — rollover % not yet agreed

## 5. Earnout Mechanics

### 5.1 Earnout Philosophy

Earnouts bridge valuation gaps on forward-looking projections (revenue, EBITDA, or milestone-based). They create contingent consideration that is taxable and accounted for separately from base consideration.

### 5.2 Earnout Structure

| Parameter | Proposed Terms |
|---|---|
| **Total earnout pool** | Up to [X]% of base purchase price |
| **Measurement period** | 12–24 months post-Closing |
| **Metric(s)** | Primary: Revenue; Secondary: Gross Margin % floor |
| **Threshold** | 0% earned below [Base Case × 80%] |
| **Target** | 100% earned at [Base Case] |
| **Stretch** | Up to [120%] at [Base Case × 115%] |
| **Payment timing** | Within 45 days after each measurement period ends |
| **Currency** | Cash (default); Buyer may elect up to 50% in equity at FMV |
| **Acceleration** | Full acceleration on Buyer Change of Control or termination without cause of key Seller management |
| **Clawback** | None (standard market practice) |

### 5.3 Tax Treatment of Earnout

| Party | Treatment |
|---|---|
| **Seller (cash earnout)** | Instalments treated under IRC §453 (instalment sale method) unless Seller elects out; capital gain recognised as payments received |
| **Seller (equity earnout)** | Non-recognition at time of grant if structured as contingent equity under §83; ordinary income risk if treated as compensation — must distinguish investment vs. services component |
| **Buyer** | Earnout payments capitalised and amortised as additional purchase price (§197 intangibles over 15 years) or allocated to other asset classes per §1060 |
| **Imputed interest** | If earnout deferred >6 months and no stated interest, IRC §483 imputes interest; include market-rate interest provision in SPA to avoid |

### 5.4 Accounting Treatment (ASC 805)

- Earnout classified as contingent consideration; fair-valued at Closing and remeasured each period through P&L (liability-classified) or in equity (equity-classified).
- Seller management earnout tied to continued employment → probable compensation expense, not purchase price.
- Buyer must disclose range of outcomes and valuation methodology in deal footnotes.

- **Owner:** CFO + Financial Advisor + Tax Counsel
- **ETA:** Earnout schedule agreed: 2026-10-24; modelled into SPA: 2026-11-07
- **RAG:** 🟡 AMBER — metric definition under negotiation
